title: Privileged intents need review at 10,000 users, not at 100 servers
plainAnswer: The trigger is 10,000 unique users who can see your app across all its servers. Server count no longer matters: under 10,000 users you toggle the intents on, at 10,000 you must apply for continued access.
quote: When an app has more than 10,000 unique users who can see your app across all the servers it's in, it requires review for continued access to Privileged Intents. Once you hit this threshold, the app or team owner will receive a system DM and/or an email.
resolution: The gateway page and the June 10, 2026 change log carry the current rule: 10,000 unique users. The application flags table on the same docs site still encodes the pre June 2026 100 server rule and was not updated. The change log is newer and explicit, so 10,000 users wins and server count is irrelevant.

title: Application flags table still says intents are required at 100 or more servers
plainAnswer: The flags table is stale. It describes the rule that applied before June 10, 2026 and must not be used to decide whether you need to apply.
quote: GATEWAY_MESSAGE_CONTENT | Intent required for bots in **100 or more servers** to receive message content
resolution: The gateway page and the June 10, 2026 change log carry the current rule: 10,000 unique users. The application flags table on the same docs site still encodes the pre June 2026 100 server rule and was not updated. The change log is newer and explicit, so 10,000 users wins and server count is irrelevant.

title: Discord's announcement: the threshold is now user count, not server count
plainAnswer: Since the announcement, apps under 10,000 users toggle intents on in the Developer Portal and apps at 10,000 users must apply for access.
quote: Starting today, the threshold is based on the number of users your app can access across all the servers it belongs to. If your app has fewer than 10,000 users, you can continue accessing Privileged Intents by toggling them on in the Developer Portal. Once your app reaches 10,000 users, you'll need to apply for Privileged Intent access.
resolution: The gateway page and the June 10, 2026 change log carry the current rule: 10,000 unique users. The application flags table on the same docs site still encodes the pre June 2026 100 server rule and was not updated. The change log is newer and explicit, so 10,000 users wins and server count is irrelevant.

title: Before June 10, 2026: intents were self-serve under 100 servers and needed an application at 100+
plainAnswer: Until June 9, 2026 an app in fewer than 100 servers could toggle privileged intents on, and an app in 100 or more servers had to apply, a process tied to verification.
quote: Previously, apps in fewer than 100 servers could access Privileged Intents by toggling them on in the Developer Portal, and apps in 100+ servers needed to apply for access.

title: 2020: presence data was unrestricted until 100 guilds, then required an application
plainAnswer: The original 100 guild threshold came from the 2020 Gateway Intents announcement for Presence Update events. It stopped applying on June 10, 2026.
quote: You may operate unrestricted on Discord until you join 100 guilds

title: Under 10,000 users: just toggle the intent on, no approval and no verification
plainAnswer: If fewer than 10,000 unique users can see your app, enable the intent on the Bot page in the Developer Portal. There is nothing to apply for and verification is irrelevant.
quote: Apps with fewer than 10,000 users can access privileged intents by enabling them in the Developer Portal.
resolution: Two paragraphs on the same gateway page disagree. The 'fewer than 10,000 users can access privileged intents by enabling them' paragraph matches the June 10, 2026 change log and the announcement that separated App Verification from intent review, so it wins. The info box and bullet that say 'after your app is verified, you can apply' are pre June 2026 text. Under 10,000 users: toggle it on, no approval, verification irrelevant. Over 10,000: apply within 90 days, verification still irrelevant.

title: Gateway info box still says Message Content is approved after verification
plainAnswer: This text predates June 10, 2026. Verification and intent review are now separate, and under 10,000 users there is no approval step at all.
quote: Like other privileged intents, `MESSAGE_CONTENT` must be approved for your app. After your app is verified, you can apply for the intent from your app's settings within the Developer Portal.
resolution: Two paragraphs on the same gateway page disagree. The 'fewer than 10,000 users can access privileged intents by enabling them' paragraph matches the June 10, 2026 change log and the announcement that separated App Verification from intent review, so it wins. The info box and bullet that say 'after your app is verified, you can apply' are pre June 2026 text. Under 10,000 users: toggle it on, no approval, verification irrelevant. Over 10,000: apply within 90 days, verification still irrelevant.

title: Gateway intents bullet still says verification is required for apps in 100+ guilds
plainAnswer: Stale line from before June 10, 2026. Verification is no longer tied to intents or to guild count.
quote: For verified apps (required for apps in 100+ guilds), the intent must also be approved after the verification process to use the intent.
resolution: Two paragraphs on the same gateway page disagree. The 'fewer than 10,000 users can access privileged intents by enabling them' paragraph matches the June 10, 2026 change log and the announcement that separated App Verification from intent review, so it wins. The info box and bullet that say 'after your app is verified, you can apply' are pre June 2026 text. Under 10,000 users: toggle it on, no approval, verification irrelevant. quote: Today, we're announcing changes to how Discord Apps access Privileged Intent with a new user-based threshold for when access requires review and an annual process to reapply for continued access.

resolution: We rule June 10, 2026. The change log entry is dated June 10, 2026 and the review guide says 'As of June 10th, 2026'. title: At 10,000 users you get 90 days from the notification to apply
plainAnswer: When you cross 10,000 users Discord notifies you by email, system DM and a Developer Portal alert. You have 90 days to submit; miss it and the intents are removed, though you can apply again at any time.
quote: You will have **90 days** from the date of the notification to submit your application. If you do not apply within this window, your app's access to Privileged Intents will be removed. You can still apply at any time to request access again.
sourceAnchor: How we count users for your app

title: Your intents keep working while your application is under review
plainAnswer: Submitting inside the 90 day window keeps your current intent access live during the review.
quote: If you submit your request during the 90-day window, your app will retain its current intent access while your submission is under review.

title: Access granted through a past review must be renewed every year
plainAnswer: If your intents were approved in a prior review (for example in 2023), you must reapply annually. Discord notifies you first, then you have 90 days; do not reapply before the notice arrives.
quote: If your app already has Privileged Intent access granted from a prior review, you're good for now, but you will need to reapply annually.

title: Discord does not show your app's user count
plainAnswer: There is no user count in the Developer Portal. Discord counts unique users across all servers the app is installed in, and tells you when you cross 10,000 with a portal alert plus email or system DM. The server install count shown under Privileged Gateway Intents is a different metric.
quote: We don’t display your app’s user count in the Developer Portal. When your app grows beyond the 10,000-user threshold and triggers Privileged Intents access review, you’ll see an alert in the Developer Portal and receive a notification via email and/or system DM.

title: Discord staff: the portal's install count and the intents install count are different numbers
plainAnswer: The General Information install count is the broadest metric. The number Discord used for intents was the smaller server bot install count under Privileged Gateway Intents. Since June 2026 the real trigger is users, which is not shown at all.
quote: there's a discrepancy between the install count reported on the General Information page vs the install count used for privileged intents. The install count reported in General Information is the most expansive version of the metric, and is meant to give developers a rough idea of their total reach.

title: Before June 2026 the portal opened intent applications at 75 servers and required them at 100
plainAnswer: The old portal strings used two numbers: 75 servers to be allowed to apply, 100 servers where approval became mandatory. Both are obsolete since June 10, 2026.
quote: This application is not currently in the minimum number of servers required for intent verification, please try again once in 75 servers.

title: Message Content became a privileged intent on September 1, 2022
plainAnswer: From September 1, 2022 message content fields are empty unless the intent is enabled, and verified or verification eligible apps had to be approved for it.
quote: As of today, message content is a privileged intent for all verified apps and apps eligible for verification.

title: February 2022 notice: Message Content to become privileged for verified bots in 75+ servers on August 31, 2022
plainAnswer: The announced date was August 31, 2022 and the threshold wording was 75+ servers. The change log then recorded it as in effect on September 1, 2022.
quote: `MESSAGE_CONTENT` is becoming a privileged intent for verified bots in 75+ servers **on August 31, 2022**.

title: Without the intent you still get content for: your own messages, DMs, mentions, and context menu targets
plainAnswer: The gateway page lists four exceptions. It does not mention replies.
quote:
Apps **without** the intent will receive empty values in fields that contain user-inputted content with a few exceptions:

* Content in messages that an app sends
* Content in DMs with the app
* Content in which the app is mentioned
* Content of the message a message context menu command is used on
resolution: Three official lists differ. We give the union: messages the app sends, DMs with the app, messages that mention the app, replies to a regular bot message when the user has ping on reply enabled (not replies to slash command responses), and the target message of a message context menu command. The reply exception appears only in the June 2026 guide and the context menu exception only on the gateway page; each page is incomplete rather than wrong.

title: The June 2026 guide adds replies (with ping on reply) as a content exception and omits context menu targets
plainAnswer: The guide lists own messages, DMs, mentions, and replies to a regular bot message when the user has ping on reply enabled. Replies to slash command responses are not covered.
quote:
The Message Content intent is **not** needed for your app to access message content in these situations:

* **Messages your app sends**
* **Direct Messages sent to your app**
* **Messages that @mention your app**
* **Replies to your app's messages.** Note: this applies to replies sent using Discord's reply feature to a regular bot message (not an interaction response) and the user has "ping on reply" enabled. It does not apply to replies to slash command responses.
resolution: Three official lists differ. We give the union: messages the app sends, DMs with the app, messages that mention the app, replies to a regular bot message when the user has ping on reply enabled (not replies to slash command responses), and the target message of a message context menu command. The reply exception appears only in the June 2026 guide and the context menu exception only on the gateway page; each page is incomplete rather than wrong.

title: The 2022 change log lists only three exceptions: own messages, DMs, mentions
plainAnswer: The original 2022 entry names three exceptions. Later pages added replies and context menu targets.
quote: These restrictions do not apply for messages that a bot or app sends, in DMs that it receives, or in messages in which it is mentioned.
resolution: Three official lists differ. We give the union: messages the app sends, DMs with the app, messages that mention the app, replies to a regular bot message when the user has ping on reply enabled (not replies to slash command responses), and the target message of a message context menu command. The reply exception appears only in the June 2026 guide and the context menu exception only on the gateway page; each page is incomplete rather than wrong.

title: Close code 4014 means you passed an intent that is not enabled or not approved
plainAnswer: 4014 is Disallowed intent(s): the toggle is off in the portal, or over 10,000 users you have not been granted it. Fix the toggle or apply. 4013 is a different error for an invalid bitfield.
quote: You sent a disallowed intent for a Gateway Intent. You may have tried to specify an intent that you have not enabled or are not approved for.

title: Support: under 10,000 users you use privileged intents without applying, so there is no 'approved' state
plainAnswer: Below 10,000 users there is no application and no approval; you turn the intents on from the Bot page.
quote: Note that apps with fewer than 10,000 users can use Privileged Intents without needing to apply; just turn them on from the bot’s page on the Developer Portal.
resolution: Ambiguous, not a hard contradiction. The checklist's 'approved for' Message Content is a state that since June 10, 2026 exists only for apps above 10,000 users. A sub 10,000 user prefix command bot has the intent but was never approved, so the checklist text does not cover it. Use slash commands to be safe, or ask developer support before enabling Premium Apps.

title: App Verification and Privileged Intent review are separate processes
plainAnswer: Since June 10, 2026, being verified neither grants nor is required for privileged intents. They are two different reviews.
quote: Previously, App Verification and Privileged Intent review were part of the same review process. With this change, we have separated App Verification and the Privileged Intent review process.
resolution: Two paragraphs on the same gateway page disagree. The 'fewer than 10,000 users can access privileged intents by enabling them' paragraph matches the June 10, 2026 change log and the announcement that separated App Verification from intent review, so it wins. The info box and bullet that say 'after your app is verified, you can apply' are pre June 2026 text. Under 10,000 users: toggle it on, no approval, verification irrelevant. Over 10,000: apply within 90 days, verification still irrelevant.

title: Support article still says verification is required to scale past 100 servers
plainAnswer: This sentence was written in 2024, before the June 2026 change. No current page confirms a 100 server cap for unverified apps, so treat it as unresolved and ask Discord support.
quote: Verification is required for your app to scale past 100 servers.
resolution: Unresolved. The June 10, 2026 announcement says growth is no longer blocked during intent review and that verification is a separate process, and the Discovery docs describe verification only as the prerequisite for Discovery and monetisation. But no current page retracts the 100 server cap for unverified apps either; the only page that states it was last edited 2024-08-30. Our ruling: cite both, say no current source states a cap, and recommend asking developer support.

title: Hitting the threshold no longer blocks your app from joining new servers
plainAnswer: Since June 10, 2026 an app under intent review keeps joining servers and reaching new users. The old block at 100 servers is gone.
quote:
Previously, when an app hit 100 servers and was required to apply for continued access to its Privileged Intents, it was blocked from joining new servers until the review was complete.

That's no longer the case. Under the new user-based threshold, apps can continue joining servers and reaching new users while their submission is under review.
resolution: Unresolved. The June 10, 2026 announcement says growth is no longer blocked during intent review and that verification is a separate process, and the Discovery docs describe verification only as the prerequisite for Discovery and monetisation. But no current page retracts the 100 server cap for unverified apps either; the only page that states it was last edited 2024-08-30. Our ruling: cite both, say no current source states a cap, and recommend asking developer support.

title: What verification unlocks: Discovery (App Directory) and monetisation
plainAnswer: Verification is the prerequisite for enabling Discovery and for Premium Apps. It is not a prerequisite for privileged intents or for growing past any server count.
quote: **App Verification** also allows you to add monetization features to your app, such as in-app purchases and subscriptions.
resolution: Unresolved. The June 10, 2026 announcement says growth is no longer blocked during intent review and that verification is a separate process, and the Discovery docs describe verification only as the prerequisite for Discovery and monetisation. But no current page retracts the 100 server cap for unverified apps either; the only page that states it was last edited 2024-08-30. Our ruling: cite both, say no current source states a cap, and recommend asking developer support.

title: To verify, the team owner must verify their identity through Stripe
plainAnswer: The owner of the team that owns the app submits a qualifying ID to Stripe, then completes the App Verification checklist in the Developer Portal.
quote: The most noteworthy requirement is that the owner of the development team which owns the app will need to verify their identity through Stripe, our identity verification provider.

title: 'Verified Bot' badge and 'verified app' are the same thing; the API flag is VERIFIED_BOT (1 << 16)
plainAnswer: The user flag VERIFIED_BOT is the badge a verified app's bot user shows. VERIFIED_DEVELOPER (1 << 17) is the legacy Early Verified Bot Developer badge. The Active Developer Badge is unrelated and decommissioned.
quote: `1 << 16` | VERIFIED_BOT | Verified Bot

title: The Active Developer Badge no longer exists
plainAnswer: The Active Developer Badge was decommissioned and removed from profiles. It was never related to App Verification.
quote: The Active Developer Badge has been decommissioned and is no longer available to earn. Any Active Developer Badges that were previously displayed on user profiles have been removed.

title: How long can I keep API data? Only as long as necessary for your stated functionality; no fixed number
plainAnswer: There is no numeric retention window in any Discord document. You must delete API data promptly once it is no longer necessary for your app's stated (and, if reviewed, approved) functionality, when you shut down, when Discord asks, or when the user asks.
quote: you will (1) promptly update the API Data upon request from us or the applicable user, and (2) promptly delete the API Data when: (a) retaining it is no longer necessary for your Application’s stated (and approved through App Review, as applicable) functionality that is permitted under the Terms; (b) you stop operating your Application (whether on your own, due to an enforcement action by us, or otherwise); (c) we request you delete it; (d) the applicable user requests you delete it; or (e) required by applicable laws or regulations.

title: 2022 Developer Terms: delete API data when no longer necessary (same wording as 2024)
plainAnswer: Between October 1, 2022 and July 7, 2024 the retention duty was worded exactly as it is today: delete promptly when no longer necessary for stated functionality.
quote: you will (1) promptly update the API Data upon request from us or the applicable user, and (2) promptly delete the API Data when: (a) retaining it is no longer necessary for your Application’s stated (and approved through App Review, as applicable) functionality that is permitted under the Terms;

title: 2020 Developer Policy: do not retain data longer than necessary for the operation of your application
plainAnswer: From July 1, 2020 to September 30, 2022 the rule was a single bullet: no retention beyond what the operation of your application needs.
quote: retain data any longer than necessary for the operation of your application;

title: 2017 Developer Terms: delete End User Data within seven days of account termination; keep chat logs only as needed
plainAnswer: The 2017 terms are the only version with a number: seven days after the user terminates their account. Chat logs could be kept only as necessary for the operation of your application.
quote: You shall delete all End User Data upon Discord’s or the End User’s request and within seven (7) days following the End User’s termination of the End User’s account. You may only retain chat logs as necessary for the operation of your Applications.

title: Can I store user IDs and message content? Yes, if it is necessary for your stated functionality
plainAnswer: Storing user IDs or content is allowed only as needed for your app's stated (and, if reviewed, approved) functionality. No Discord policy forbids storing user IDs; the purpose limit is what matters, and improvement use needs aggregated or de-identified data.
quote: You may not request, access, or use API Data for any purpose other than as necessary to provide your Application’s stated (and approved through App Review, as applicable) functionality; provided that you may also use API Data for the purpose of improving your Application only if it has been aggregated or de-identified such that it cannot be associated with, or used to identify, any individual.

title: Every app needs a privacy policy, even a bot in one private server
plainAnswer: The Developer Terms apply to every Application. You must provide and follow a privacy policy that describes what you collect, how you use and share it, and how users can request deletion, and keep a public link to it in the Developer Portal.
quote: You will provide and adhere to a privacy policy for your Application that is compliant with applicable privacy laws and clearly, accurately, and fully describes to users of your Application what data you collect, how you use and share such data with us and third parties, and how users can request deletion of such data.

title: API data must be encrypted at rest
plainAnswer: Whatever you store from the API must be encrypted at rest and protected by administrative, physical and technical safeguards.
quote: These efforts will include: (i) encryption of the data at rest and (ii) maintaining administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that are designed to prevent unauthorized access and use and comply with applicable laws and regulations (including relating to data security and privacy).

title: You may not train ML or AI models on message content without Discord's express permission
plainAnswer: Fine tuning an LLM on message content your bot collected is banned unless Discord grants express permission. The rule was added in the July 8, 2024 policy; the October 1, 2022 version had no such rule.
quote: **21. Do not use message content obtained through the APIs to train machine learning or AI models (including large language models) unless express permission is granted by Discord.**

title: Do not DM users without their explicit permission
plainAnswer: A welcome DM on join is unsolicited unless the user themselves opted in. A server owner enabling a feature is not the user's permission; keep DMs tied to functionality the user triggered.
quote: **5. Do not contact users on Discord without their explicit permission.** This includes frequently sending unsolicited direct messages and/or sending direct messages not directly related to maintaining or improving an Application's functionality.

title: Do not target users with advertisements or marketing
plainAnswer: Messages from your app must be relevant to its function. Promotional content unrelated to the app is banned.
quote: **6. Do not target users with advertisements or marketing.** Messaging to Discord users from any Application or developer team should be relevant to the function of the Application and may not contain material unrelated to an Application’s function or information.

title: In intent review you must explain why you store data and describe your retention policy
plainAnswer: If you store data from privileged intents, the review form expects the reason, the retention policy and the security measures. Processing in memory and discarding is an acceptable answer.
quote: If you're storing the data, explain why it's necessary and describe your retention policy and security measures. If you're processing it in memory and discarding it, say so.

title: What a bot sees with zero privileged intents: profiles, roles, message metadata, voice state, reactions, locale
plainAnswer: Every bot gets a baseline: usernames, avatars, banners, nicknames, roles, message metadata such as time sent, voice channel joins and voice state, reactions, and members' language setting. The article still lists discriminators, which were removed in 2023. Content fields need Message Content; join and leave events need Guild Members; status needs Presence.

title: Discord's Privacy Policy tells users that popular apps must apply for access to certain data
plainAnswer: The user facing Privacy Policy states the intent review system exists and that developers must have a privacy policy. It gives no threshold; the developer docs supply the 10,000 user number.
quote: We also require that certain popular apps apply for access to certain data.

title: Current Developer Policy: effective July 8, 2024, last updated June 6, 2024
plainAnswer: The Developer Policy in force today took effect on July 8, 2024. It replaced the October 1, 2022 version.
quote:
Effective date: July 8, 2024

Last updated: June 6, 2024

title: 2022 Developer Policy: effective October 1, 2022, last updated September 1, 2022
plainAnswer: From October 1, 2022 to July 7, 2024 the 2022 Developer Policy applied. It has no rule about training AI models.
quote:
*Effective: October 1, 2022*

*Last Updated: September 1, 2022*

title: Current Developer Terms of Service: effective July 8, 2024, last updated June 6, 2024
plainAnswer: The Developer Terms in force today took effect on July 8, 2024, the same day as the current Developer Policy.
quote:
*Effective date: July 8, 2024*

*Last updated: June 6, 2024*

title: 2022 Developer Terms of Service: effective October 1, 2022
plainAnswer: From October 1, 2022 to July 7, 2024 the 2022 Developer Terms applied.
quote: *Effective date: October 1, 2022*

title: 2020 Developer Terms of Service: effective August 18, 2020
plainAnswer: From August 18, 2020 to September 30, 2022 the 2020 Developer Terms applied.
quote: **Effective date: August 18, 2020**

title: 2017 Developer Terms of Service: effective August 20, 2017
plainAnswer: Before August 18, 2020 the 2017 Developer Terms applied.
quote: **Effective Date: August 20, 2017**

title: Arbitration opt out: within 30 days of July 8, 2024 or of creating your first Application
plainAnswer: US based developers can opt out of arbitration by email within 30 days of July 8, 2024 or of first creating an Application, whichever is later.
quote: the date for emailing an opt-out notice is within 30 days of July 8, 2024 or when you first create an Application, whichever is later.
sourceAnchor: Section 12(e): Choice of Law; Dispute Resolution

title: Discord's Terms of Service bind apps to the Developer Terms and Developer Policy
plainAnswer: The user facing Terms (effective September 29, 2025) state that third party apps must follow the Developer Terms of Service and Developer Policy, and that Discord is not responsible for them.
quote: While these third parties do need to follow all policies that apply to them (which may include these Terms, our Community Guidelines, Developer Terms of Service, and Developer Policy), Discord is not responsible for any third-party services.

title: Global rate limit: 50 requests per second per bot
plainAnswer: Your bot can make 50 requests per second across the API, independent of per route limits. Without an authorization header the limit applies per IP.
quote: All bots can make up to 50 requests per second to our API. If no authorization header is provided, then the limit is applied to the IP address. This is independent of any individual rate limit on a route.

title: Interaction endpoints are exempt from the global rate limit, ephemeral or not
plainAnswer: Responding to, following up on and editing interaction responses does not count against the 50 per second global limit. Per route and shared limits still apply, and ephemerality changes nothing.
quote: Interaction endpoints are not bound to the bot's Global Rate Limit.
resolution: The developer docs win (authority 80 over 60) and are precise: all interaction endpoints, ephemeral or not, are exempt from the global 50 per second limit only; per route and shared limits still apply. The support article's 'ephemeral messages do not count towards the rate limits' is narrower (ephemeral only) and broader (all limits) at the same time, and wrong on both counts.

title: Support article says ephemeral interaction responses do not count towards the rate limits
plainAnswer: Wrong on scope. The docs exempt all interaction endpoints from the global limit only; ephemerality is irrelevant and per route limits still apply.
quote: Bonus tip: Make Interaction Responses and follow-up messages ephemeral since they do not count towards the rate limits.
resolution: The developer docs win (authority 80 over 60) and are precise: all interaction endpoints, ephemeral or not, are exempt from the global 50 per second limit only; per route and shared limits still apply. The support article's 'ephemeral messages do not count towards the rate limits' is narrower (ephemeral only) and broader (all limits) at the same time, and wrong on both counts.

title: 10,000 invalid requests in 10 minutes gets your IP temporarily banned by Cloudflare
plainAnswer: 401, 403 and 429 responses count as invalid (except 429s with X-RateLimit-Scope: shared). Over 10,000 in 10 minutes and the IP is temporarily blocked.
quote: IP addresses that make too many invalid HTTP requests are automatically and temporarily restricted from accessing the Discord API. Currently, this limit is **10,000 per 10 minutes**. An invalid request is one that results in **401**, **403**, or **429** statuses.

title: retry_after is seconds (float) on API v8 and later; the Retry-After header is integer seconds
plainAnswer: Sleep for retry_after seconds. A value of 2.5 means two and a half seconds, not milliseconds. This has been true since API v8 on September 24, 2020 and applies to v8, v9 and v10.
quote: retry_after | float | The number of seconds to wait before submitting another request.
resolution: Seconds. The developer docs (authority 80) and the September 24, 2020 API v8 change log entry both say seconds, and the docs example pairs Retry-After: 65 with retry_after: 64.57. The support article (authority 60, edited 2025-07-14) kept the pre v8 milliseconds wording. Sleeping for milliseconds re-hits the limit and counts toward the 10,000 invalid requests per 10 minutes ban.

title: Support article says retry_after is milliseconds
plainAnswer: Wrong for every supported API version. This is the pre v8 unit that the support article never updated.
quote: `retry_after`: Milliseconds to wait before making another request
sourceAnchor: How to Identify Your Rate Limit Issue
resolution: Seconds. The developer docs (authority 80) and the September 24, 2020 API v8 change log entry both say seconds, and the docs example pairs Retry-After: 65 with retry_after: 64.57. The support article (authority 60, edited 2025-07-14) kept the pre v8 milliseconds wording. Sleeping for milliseconds re-hits the limit and counts toward the 10,000 invalid requests per 10 minutes ban.

title: API v8 (September 24, 2020) switched retry_after from milliseconds to seconds
plainAnswer: The change log records the unit change: since v8, Retry-After and retry_after are in seconds.
quote: The `Retry-After` header value and `retry_after` body value is now based in seconds instead of milliseconds (e.g. `123` means 123 seconds)

title: Sharding is mandatory at 2,500 guilds
plainAnswer: Each shard can serve at most 2,500 guilds, so at 2,500 or more guilds you must shard. Get Gateway Bot returns a recommended shard count.
quote: Each shard can only support a maximum of 2500 guilds, and apps that are in 2500+ guilds *must* enable sharding.

title: Support: plan sharding at 2,000 guilds, mandatory at 2,500, about 1 shard per 1,000 guilds
plainAnswer: Consistent with the docs: sharding must be on at 2,500 guilds; the recommended ratio is roughly one shard per 1,000 guilds.
quote: It's recommended to start planning for sharding implementation when approaching 2,000 guilds, as sharding **must** be enabled at 2,500+ guilds. For optimal performance, follow the best practice of maintaining approximately 1 shard per 1,000 guilds.

title: Over 150,000 guilds Discord moves you to large bot sharding
plainAnswer: Near 150,000 guilds Discord migrates the bot to large bot sharding, assigns a shard number that your shard count must be a multiple of, and raises the session start limit to max(2000, guild_count / 1000 * 5) per day.
quote: If your bot is in more than 150,000 guilds, there are some additional considerations you must take around sharding. Discord will migrate your bot to large bot sharding when it starts to get near the large bot sharding threshold.

title: 1,000 IDENTIFY calls per 24 hours across all shards; exceeding it resets your token
plainAnswer: The IDENTIFY limit is 1,000 per day globally across shards (RESUME does not count). Hitting it terminates all sessions, resets the bot token and emails the owner.
quote: Clients are limited to 1000 `IDENTIFY` calls to the websocket in a 24-hour period. This limit is global and across all shards, but does not include `RESUME` calls. Upon hitting this limit, all active sessions for the app will be terminated, the bot token will be reset, and the owner will receive an email notification.

title: Command quotas: 100 global chat input, 15 user, 15 message, 1 entry point; same per guild
plainAnswer: An app can register 100 global CHAT_INPUT commands, 15 global USER commands, 15 global MESSAGE commands and 1 PRIMARY_ENTRY_POINT command, and the same counts per guild for guild commands.
quote:
* 100 global `CHAT_INPUT` commands
* 15 global `USER` commands
* 15 global `MESSAGE` commands
* 1 global `PRIMARY_ENTRY_POINT` command

title: 200 command creates per day per guild
plainAnswer: Creating commands is rate limited to 200 per day per guild. Register once at startup, not on every reconnect.
quote: There is a global rate limit of 200 application command creates per day, per guild

title: Respond to an interaction within 3 seconds; the token lives 15 minutes
plainAnswer: You must send an initial response within 3 seconds or the interaction token is invalidated. After that you have 15 minutes for follow ups.
quote: Interaction `tokens` are valid for **15 minutes** and can be used to send followup messages but you **must send an initial response within 3 seconds of receiving the event**. If the 3 second deadline is exceeded, the token will be invalidated.

title: Default file upload limit is 20 MiB per file (since September 2026)
plainAnswer: Bots, webhooks and interaction responses can upload 20 MiB per file by default, more when the user's Nitro or the server's boost tier allows. Between January 16, 2025 and early September 2026 the default was 10 MiB.
quote: The file upload size limit applies to each file in a request. The default limit is `20 MiB` for all users, but may be higher for users depending on their Nitro status or by the server's Boost Tier.

title: Change log: default upload limit raised from 10 MiB to 20 MiB for users, bots, webhooks and interactions
plainAnswer: The change log entry labelled September 3, 2026 records the increase. GitHub issue 8572 shows the API and docs caught up with the user support article by September 5, 2026.
quote: The default file upload limit has been increased from 10 MiB to 20 MiB for users, bots, webhooks, and interaction responses!

title: January 16, 2025: default upload limit dropped from 25 MiB to 10 MiB
plainAnswer: From January 16, 2025 until the September 2026 increase, the default per file limit was 10 MiB.
quote: On January 16, 2025, the default file upload limit will change from 25 MiB to 10 MiB.

title: Discord staff: support articles describe user functionality, not bot functionality
plainAnswer: When a support.discord.com article and the developer docs disagree about what bots can do, the developer docs describe what bots get. Discord staff said this in the September 2026 upload limit issue.
quote: The API docs still list the 10 mb limit. Once bots get the 20 mb limit the docs will be updated. Support articles reflect functionality for users, not bots.

title: Premium Apps eligibility: verified app, owned by a team, owner 18+, emails verified and 2FA, slash commands or approved Message Content, ToS and privacy links
plainAnswer: To enable monetisation the app must be verified and owned by a team whose owner is at least 18 with verified emails and 2FA on; the app must use slash commands or have approved Message Content, link a Terms of Service and a Privacy Policy, have clean naming, payouts set up, and accept the Monetization Terms and Developer Policy.
quote:
* App must be verified
* App belongs to a developer team
* Team owner must be at least 18 years old
* Team must have verified emails and 2FA set up
* App uses slash commands, or has been approved for the privileged `Message Content` intent
* App has a link to your Terms of Service

title: Monetisation checklist: app must use slash commands or be approved for Message Content
plainAnswer: The checklist accepts slash commands, or an approved Message Content intent. Since June 10, 2026 approval only exists above 10,000 users, so a prefix command bot under 10,000 users is not clearly covered.
quote: App uses slash commands, or has been approved for the privileged `Message Content` intent
resolution: Ambiguous, not a hard contradiction. The checklist's 'approved for' Message Content is a state that since June 10, 2026 exists only for apps above 10,000 users. A sub 10,000 user prefix command bot has the intent but was never approved, so the checklist text does not cover it. Use slash commands to be safe, or ask developer support before enabling Premium Apps.

title: Premium Apps is only available to teams based in the US, UK or EU
plainAnswer: If your team owner is outside the United States, the United Kingdom or the European Union you cannot enable Premium Apps yet.
quote: Premium Apps is not currently available outside of these regions. These features will be made available to more regions soon.
sourceAnchor: #step-3-set-up-team-payouts (If You are Based Outside of the United States, European Union, or United Kingdom)

title: Supported locales for Premium Apps: United States, United Kingdom, European Union (all 27 member states)
plainAnswer: The support article lists the US, the UK and every EU member state. Canada, India, Brazil and other countries are not supported.
quote:
* United States
* United Kingdom
* European Union

title: Docs: you become eligible for payout after your first $100
plainAnswer: The developer docs state the threshold as $100 made, without saying whether fees are deducted first.
quote: Once your app has made its first $100 it will become eligible for payout.
resolution: The support article is more specific: the $100 is net of payment processing and transaction fees, then $25 minimum per cycle, paid within 45 days after month end. The docs sentence is a simplification of the same rule, not a different rule. Answer with the net figure and cite both.

title: Support: payout eligibility starts at $100 earned net of processing and transaction fees
plainAnswer: The $100 threshold is counted after payment processing and transaction fees. $100 of gross sales may not be enough.
quote: your team will become eligible for payout review after the first 100 dollars is earned [less applicable payment processing fees and transaction fees].
resolution: The support article is more specific: the $100 is net of payment processing and transaction fees, then $25 minimum per cycle, paid within 45 days after month end. The docs sentence is a simplification of the same rule, not a different rule. Answer with the net figure and cite both.

title: Payouts arrive within 45 days after month end; $25 minimum per cycle, smaller balances roll over
plainAnswer: After the first $100 net, each later cycle pays out only amounts above $25, within 45 days after the end of the calendar month. Under $25 rolls over to the next cycle.
quote: Eligible payouts will be provided within 45 days after the end of each calendar month. For example, for offerings purchased in January, you will receive payouts within 45 days after January 31st. An eligible payout can be defined as the first $100 earned [less applicable payment processing fees and transaction fees] and for the following billing cycles, in amounts greater than $25.

title: Since October 7, 2024 paid features must also be sold through Premium Apps at no higher price (US, UK, EU)
plainAnswer: If you sell premium features anywhere (Patreon, your website) and your team is in a Premium Apps region, you must also offer them through Premium Apps at a price no higher than elsewhere. Outside the supported regions the rule does not bite yet.
quote:
Beginning on October 7, 2024, in regions where Discord supports monetization through its Premium Apps products, all developers who offer paid features or capabilities for their Application will be required to:

* (i) support purchase of such features or capabilities through Discord’s Premium Apps products; and,
* (ii) offer such features or capabilities at prices on Discord that are no higher than the prices at which they are offered through other payment options.

title: Up to 50 SKUs per app
plainAnswer: An app can have at most 50 SKUs in total across subscriptions and one time purchases.
quote: * You can create up to 50 total SKUs per app.

title: Discovery (App Directory) requires the team owner to complete identity and app verification
plainAnswer: You cannot enable Discovery until the team owner has verified their identity through Stripe and the app has passed App Verification. Then complete the Discovery Status checklist and metadata in the Developer Portal.
quote: To enable **Discovery** for your app, we require your team owner to complete identity and application verification.

title: After enabling Discovery it can take up to 24 hours to appear
plainAnswer: Once enabled, allow up to 24 hours for the app to show in the App Directory and App Launcher.
quote: Once you enable **Discovery**, it may take up to 24 hours for your app to appear in the App Directory and App Launcher.

title: App Directory content must be appropriate for ages 13+
plainAnswer: No graphic violence, sexual content or other age restricted topics in a discoverable app; it must suit all ages 13 and up.
quote: **3. Do not host graphic or sexual content.** Graphic violence, sexual content, or other age-restricted topics are not allowed in public spaces. Apps opting into discoverability should be appropriate for audiences of all ages 13+.

title: A bot token is shown once; if you lose it you must reset it
plainAnswer: The Developer Portal shows the token only once. After leaving the page the copy button is gone and the only way back is Reset Token, which invalidates the old token.
quote: You won't be able to view your token again unless you regenerate it, so make sure to keep it somewhere safe (like in a password manager).

title: Reset Token lives on the Bot page and may ask for your 2FA code
plainAnswer: Bot page, Reset Token under Build-a-Bot, confirm, enter your two factor code if prompted, then copy the new token straight into your config. The old token stops working.
quote:
Press the **Reset Token** button located under the **Build-a-Bot** section.
4. A pop-up window will show up asking you to confirm.
5. Enter your Two-Factor Authentication code, if requested.
sourceAnchor: How to Regenerate the Bot's Token

title: Tokens must be kept encrypted and never embedded in open source projects
plainAnswer: Keep API keys and tokens encrypted in any file third parties can reach, and never commit developer credentials to an open source repository.
quote: you will keep API keys and tokens encrypted in any files or other materials accessible by third parties (other than your Service Providers, subject to Section 12(a)). For the avoidance of doubt, developer credentials may not be embedded in open source projects.

title: Self-bots and user-bots are banned by the Community Guidelines (rule 14)
plainAnswer: Automating a user account, even for a private tool, violates Community Guidelines rule 14. Only bot accounts (an Application with a bot user) may automate.
quote: **14. Do not use self-bots or user-bots.** Each account must be associated with a human, not a bot.

title: Support: automating a normal user account outside the OAuth2 and bot API can get the account terminated
plainAnswer: Discord's stance since 2017: self-bots are forbidden and can result in account termination.
quote: Automating normal user accounts (generally called "self-bots") outside of the OAuth2/bot API is forbidden, and can result in an account termination if found.

title: Global slash commands need the applications.commands scope, which the bot scope includes
plainAnswer: Add applications.commands to your install link, or just use the bot scope, which includes it by default.
quote: applications.commands | allows your app to add commands to a guild - included by default with the `bot` scope

title: Bots with elevated permissions need 2FA on the owner's account in servers with server-wide 2FA
plainAnswer: If your bot requests a permission marked with an asterisk (for example Ban Members, Manage Guild) and the server has server-wide 2FA on, the bot owner's account must have two factor authentication enabled.
quote: For bots with elevated permissions (permissions with a `*` next to them), we enforce two-factor authentication on the owner's account when added to guilds that have server-wide 2FA enabled.

title: Under 16 article: team ownership cannot be transferred after verification
plainAnswer: Obsolete. This 2024 text says a verified team's ownership is frozen; the September 2025 transfer article documents a support ticket process that removes verification and lets the new owner re-verify.
quote: That person will need to be the owner of the team, and ownership can't be transferred after verification is complete.
sourceAnchor: I haven't verified my bot yet, and I'm under 16
resolution: The transfer article (created September 12, 2025, edited July 27, 2026) documents a support ticket process: dual consent within 30 days, verification removed, identity data deleted, new owner re-verifies. It is newer and more specific, so it wins. The Under 16 article (content from 2024) was never updated and its 'can't be transferred' is obsolete.

title: A verified app's team can be transferred, but verification is removed and the new owner re-verifies
plainAnswer: Yes, via a Developer Support ticket: the current owner requests, the recipient consents within 30 days, verification is stripped and identity data deleted, then the new owner (16+ with a Stripe qualifying ID) re-verifies.
quote: If your developer team owns verified applications, transferring ownership will require **removing verification** from those applications. The new owner will need to reapply for verification after the transfer is complete.
resolution: The transfer article (created September 12, 2025, edited July 27, 2026) documents a support ticket process: dual consent within 30 days, verification removed, identity data deleted, new owner re-verifies. It is newer and more specific, so it wins. The Under 16 article (content from 2024) was never updated and its 'can't be transferred' is obsolete.

title: Ownership transfer needs dual consent; both parties have 30 days to respond
plainAnswer: Only the current owner can request a transfer. Discord then asks the recipient to consent; if either side declines or does not respond within 30 days the request is denied. Typical total time is 30 to 60 days.
quote: After the **current owner** requests a transfer, Discord requires **consent from the recipient** before any ownership transfer. Both parties have **30 days to respond** to our requests.

title: Unverified apps move from an individual to a team with the self-serve 'Transfer App to Team' option
plainAnswer: For an unverified app you do not need a ticket: General Information, Transfer App to Team, pick the team, confirm. Verified apps need Developer Support.
quote:
If you currently own unverified applications individually and want to transfer them to your team:

1. Ensure your team has completed identity verification
2. Navigate to your application settings
3. Go to the "General Information" section

title: You must be at least 13 (or your country's minimum) to use Discord at all
plainAnswer: The platform minimum is 13, or higher where local law requires it. Discord's Terms, Privacy Policy and Community Guidelines all took effect on September 29, 2025.
quote: By accessing our services, you confirm that you’re at least 13 years old and meet the minimum age required by the laws in your country. Our services are not designed for nor directed towards users under the age of 13.

title: You must be at least 13 to accept the Developer Terms; under the age of consent a parent must agree for you
plainAnswer: Creating an Application means accepting the Developer Terms, which requires being 13 and meeting your country's minimum. If you are too young to consent, your parent or guardian agrees on your behalf and is responsible.
quote: You also confirm and agree that (i) you are at least 13 years of age and meet the minimum age required by the laws in your country, and (ii) if you are not old enough to have authority to consent to the Terms in your country, that your parent or legal guardian must agree to the Terms on your behalf.

title: The person who submits ID for verification must be 16 or over
plainAnswer: Under 16 you cannot verify on your own ID. A team owner who is 16 or over (parent, guardian, friend or co-developer) with a Stripe qualifying ID verifies on the app's behalf and must keep owning the team; you stay a member.
quote: However, the individual who applies to verify your bot will need to be 16 or over.
sourceAnchor: I haven't verified my bot yet, and I'm under 16

title: The minimum age to operate a verified bot is Discord's minimum age for your country
plainAnswer: You can run a verified bot at 13 (or your country's minimum); only the ID submitted for verification must belong to someone 16 or over.
quote: As before, the minimum age for operating a verified bot on Discord is the same as the minimum age for using Discord in your country.
sourceAnchor: I haven't verified my bot yet, and I'm under 16

title: The team owner must be at least 18 to enable monetisation
plainAnswer: Premium Apps requires the team owner to be 18 or older. Verification at 16 is not enough to monetise.
quote: * Team owner must be at least 18 years old

title: Accepting the Monetization Terms requires being at least 18
plainAnswer: The Monetization Terms (effective June 6, 2024) can only be accepted by someone who is at least 18 and meets the age of digital consent in their country.
quote: By accepting these Monetization Terms, you agree to comply with the Terms and that the Terms control your relationship with us. You also confirm and agree that you are at least 18 years of age and meet the minimum age of digital consent in your country.

title: 2026 age assurance rollout: no action expected from developers
plainAnswer: Discord's teen by default and age assurance changes roll out in the second half of 2026. Discord does not expect developers to change integrations; you keep managing age requirements for your own app.
quote: **TLDR: We do not expect any action to be required from developers.**

text: My bot is in 150 servers. Do I need to apply for the Message Content intent?
expectedAnswer: Server count is irrelevant since June 10, 2026. With about 4,000 users you are under the 10,000 user threshold: toggle Message Content on in Developer Portal > Bot > Privileged Gateway Intents, no application, no verification. At 10,000 users you get a notification and 90 days to apply. Before June 10, 2026 the answer was yes (100+ servers required application and verification). The application flags table that still says 100 or more servers is stale.
note: Stale answer: 'yes, you are over 100 servers so you must apply and verify'. That was true until June 9, 2026 and the flags table still says it.

text: How do I see how many users my app has, so I know if I'm near 10,000?
expectedAnswer: You cannot. Discord does not display the user count in the Developer Portal; it counts unique users across all servers the app is installed in and notifies you (portal alert, email or system DM) when you cross 10,000. The server bot install count under Privileged Gateway Intents is a different metric, as Discord staff admitted in GitHub issue 7806.
note: Stale answer: 'check the server count on General Information, you need approval at 100'. Server counts are the wrong metric.

text: I already got Message Content approved in 2023. Do I need to do anything?
expectedAnswer: Yes. Access granted through a prior review must be reapplied for annually. You will receive a notification, then have 90 days to reapply; access continues during review. Do not reapply before the notice arrives.
note: Stale answer: 'no, approval is permanent'. Annual reapplication started June 10, 2026.

text: I got close code 4014 when connecting. What's wrong?
expectedAnswer: 4014 is Disallowed intent(s): an intent in your IDENTIFY bitfield is not enabled in the Developer Portal (or, above 10,000 users, not granted). With 3,000 users you are under the threshold, so turn the toggle on under Bot > Privileged Gateway Intents and reconnect. Being in 120 servers is irrelevant. 4013 is a different error for an invalid bitfield.
note: Stale answer: 'you are over 100 servers so you need to get verified and approved first'.

text: Can my bot read message content without the intent if the user replies to it?
expectedAnswer: Sometimes. The gateway page adds the target message of a message context menu command and omits replies. Give the union and cite both pages.

title: Headers need a space after #, ## or ### at the start of the line
plainAnswer: A header only renders when the line starts with #, ## or ### followed by a space. '##Rules' stays literal; '## Rules' becomes a header. One # is the biggest, ### the smallest.
quote:
**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the leading heading character (`#`, `##`, `###`) and your text!

title: Subtext is -# at the very start of the line, followed by a space
plainAnswer: Put -# then a space at the very beginning of a line to render it as small grey subtext. It fails if anything precedes the -# on that line or if the space is missing.

title: Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and their combinations

| *Italics* | \*italics\* **or** \_italics\_ | *Underline italics* | \_\_\*underline italics\*\_\_ |
| **Bold** | \*\*bold\*\* | **Underline bold** | \_\_\*\*underline bold\*\*\_\_ |
| ***Bold Italics*** | \*\*\*bold italics\*\*\* | ***underline bold italics*** | \_\_\*\*\*underline bold italics\*\*\*\_\_ |
| Underline | \_\_underline\_\_ | ~~Strikethrough~~ | ~~Strikethrough~~ |

title: Spoilers are ||text||, and a code block cancels them

title: Spoiler tags article: ||text|| or /spoiler; not hidden inside code blocks

quote: You can also manually tag spoilers by using the Markdown syntax ||Insert spoilers here|| or typing /spoiler before your message.

title: Block quote: > plus a space at the start of the line
plainAnswer: Start a line with > and a space to quote that one line. Without the space it stays a literal greater-than sign.
quote:
**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the leading > and your text!

Another option is using block quotes. To use a block quote, you just need to put (`>`) at the beginning of a line of text to create a single block quote.

title: Multi line block quote: >>> before the first line quotes everything after it
plainAnswer: >>> at the start of a line turns that line and every following line of the message into one block quote. Nothing after it can leave the quote, so put >>> last if you also need normal text.
quote: If you want to add multiple lines to a single block quote, just add (`>>>`) before the first line.

title: Bulleted lists: - or * at the start of each line, then a space
plainAnswer: Start each item with - or * and a space. Numbered items use 1. and a space. Without the space the dash is literal text.
quote:
**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the list bullet (`-`, `*`, `1.`, etc) and your text!

You can create a bulleted list using either (`-`) or (`*)` in the beginning of each line.

title: Nest a list item by indenting it with 2 spaces
plainAnswer: Indent a bullet with two spaces before the - or * to make it a sub item. Discord's page shows one level of indentation.
quote: You can also indent your list by adding 2 spaces before (`-`) or (`*`) at the beginning of each line.

title: Masked links: [display text](https://url)
plainAnswer: Write the visible text in square brackets followed by the URL in parentheses. The support article presents this as ordinary chat formatting for everyone; no current Discord page restricts masked links to bots, webhooks or embeds, so do not promise a developer that users cannot send them.
quote: You can use masked links to make text a clickable or pressable hyperlink. To do so, you need to include the text you want displayed in brackets and then the URL in parentheses.

title: Inline code uses single backticks, multi line code blocks use triple backticks

A language name right after the opening fence (for example ```js) gives syntax highlighting in the client, but no Discord page we hold documents that, so treat it as client behaviour, not a rule.
quote: You can make your own code blocks by wrapping your text in backticks (`` ` ``).

| title | 256 characters |
| description | 4096 characters |
| fields | Up to 25 field objects |
| field.name | 256 characters |
| field.value | 1024 characters |
| footer.text | 2048 characters |
| author.name | 256 characters |

title: Embed limits: 6000 characters combined across all embeds, or 400 Bad Request

title: Discord may strip characters that break formatting; sanitise user strings and set allowed_mentions

title: Mentions notify according to the sender's permissions and allowed_mentions

title: Custom emoji: <:name:id>, animated: <a:name:id>, standard emoji are plain Unicode

| Animated custom emoji               | `<a:NAME:ID>`                            | `<a:b1nzy:392938283556143104>`        |

title: Timestamps: <t:UNIX> or <t:UNIX:STYLE>, in seconds, shown in each viewer's timezone
plainAnswer: Write <t:1618953630> or <t:1618953630:R>. The number is Unix seconds, not milliseconds, and every reader sees it in their own timezone and locale.
quote: Timestamps are expressed in **seconds** and display the given timestamp in the user's timezone and locale.

title: Timestamp styles: t, T, d, D, f (default), F, s, S, R (relative)
plainAnswer: Styles: t short time, T medium time, d short date, D long date, f long date with short time (the default), F full date, s short date and time, S short date and medium time, R relative like '4 years ago'.

| T     | 16:20:30                         | Medium Time             |
| d     | 20/04/2021                       | Short Date              |
| D     | April 20, 2021                   | Long Date               |
| f \*  | April 20, 2021 at 16:20          | Long Date, Short Time   |
| F     | Tuesday, April 20, 2021 at 16:20 | Full Date, Short Time   |
| s     | 20/04/2021, 16:20                | Short Date, Short Time  |
| S     | 20/04/2021, 16:20:30             | Short Date, Medium Time |
| R     | 4 years ago                      | Relative Time           |
